method: Hand-curated for the Streamer Desk (wave 29 / rotation 12) from ordinary web search on 2026-10-13. Directory facts carry at least one credible source each; drama-timeline entries carry two or more independent sources per event or are not printed as verified. Rosters are dated claims ('as of'), never eternal facts. No viewership or follower numbers are printed unless a source states them for a dated event. Wave 34 (rotation 13) follow-through: three items carried by the research streamer beat (multi-source-verified in its rounds through 2026-10-13) were added, the Jynxzi tournament and Kyedae return events and the Esports Awards 2026 nominees update; the beat's held single-source items (TwitchCon safety withdrawals, ComplexCon suspensions, a FaZe/100 Thieves event item) were NOT promoted.

sourcing_standard.directory: 1+ credible source per profile/house, named on the record.
sourcing_standard.drama: Timeline format only. An event is 'verified' only when 2+ independent credible sources report it. Single-source or disputed claims are listed under 'unverified' with the allegation labeled as an allegation, or omitted. Neutral tone; no rumor is printed as fact.
sourcing_standard.updates: 1+ credible source per dated entry; records and platform moves prefer 2.

honesty: Every profile and house carries its sources on the record. A drama event is printed as verified only when two or more independent sources report it; anything weaker is listed under unverified with the reason, or omitted. Rosters are dated 'as of' claims. No follower, viewership or revenue numbers appear except where a named source states them for a dated event. Event status is computed from dates at build time, a past event never poses as upcoming.

drama.note: Payment claims below are Ironmouse's stated allegations plus VShojo's own shutdown statement as reported; the Desk reports who said what, and the undisputed facts (departures, shutdown) as facts.

timeline.event: Ironmouse, a VShojo founding member, announced her immediate departure, alleging the agency had withheld a significant amount of her revenue, including roughly $500,000 raised for the Immune Deficiency Foundation. She said she was acting on legal advice.

VShojo's remaining talent publicly resigned in the days following Ironmouse's announcement, several making similar unpaid-revenue allegations; Ironmouse's independent IDF fundraiser passed $1M within two days.
VShojo announced it was shutting down. Its CEO took responsibility for the failure in the company's statement, as reported by multiple outlets.

drama.title: VShojo: Ironmouse's departure and the agency's shutdown

drama.note: The departures and dates are multiply reported. The alleged reason, a disputed retroactive revenue/equity demand, is a claim by departing-side commentators, is contested, and is filed under Unverified below, not in this timeline.

timeline.event: Richard 'FaZe Banks' Bengtson stepped down as CEO of FaZe Media, months after GameSquare divested its remaining FaZe Media stake (Mar 31, 2025) while keeping full ownership of FaZe Esports.
FaZe Clan posted an official roster list naming who was, and was not, FaZe: Adapt, Apex, Jason, Jev, Kaysan, Lacy, Rage, Replays, Ron, Rug, Scope, Silky, Swagg and ZooMaa, plus its pro esports teams.

Adapt, JasonTheWeen, Lacy, Silky and Stable Ronaldo each announced their departure from FaZe Clan in near-identical 'Left @FaZeClan' posts. Multiple outlets reported the exits followed failed contract talks; management said the organization would continue.

drama.note: Neutral record of a long-running case. What Beahm acknowledged, what Twitch has and has not said, and what platforms did are kept as separate facts; no outlet's characterization is adopted as the Desk's own.

timeline.event: Twitch permanently banned Dr Disrespect (Guy Beahm), months after signing him to a multi-year deal. Twitch did not publicly state a specific reason at the time, and Beahm said he had not been told one.
Beahm's legal dispute with Twitch over the ban was resolved; neither party admitted wrongdoing, and Beahm later said his contract was paid out in full.

After former Twitch staff publicly alleged the ban involved 2017 messages to a minor, Beahm posted a statement acknowledging he had exchanged messages with a minor in 2017 that he characterized as inappropriate, while maintaining nothing illegal occurred. Midnight Society, the studio he co-founded, ended its relationship with him on June 24.
YouTube suspended monetization on Beahm's channel, citing its Creator Responsibility policy, and paused paid memberships.

YouTube reinstated Beahm's monetization after a review of the channel's recent activity, having denied an earlier reapplication in Oct 2024; the platform said further violations would bring further action.

drama.title: Dr Disrespect: the 2020 Twitch ban, the 2024 disclosure, and YouTube's reversal
